questions.problem:
Find the solution to the following system of equations.

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2a+3b=-2 \\ \frac{a}{3}-\frac{b}{6}=-\frac{5}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To get rid of the fractions in the second equation, we must multiply the second equation by the lowest common denominator of the fractions, which is $6.$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2a+3b=-2 \\ \frac{a}{3}-\frac{b}{6}=-\frac{5}{3} & |\,\times 6\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}2a+3b=-2 \\ 2a-b=-10\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the substitution method to solve the system. Let's solve for $b$ in the second equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}2a-b & =-10 \\ b & =2a+10\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we can substitute $b=2a+10$ into the first equation and solve for $a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2a+3b & =-2 \\ 2a+3(2a+10) & =-2 \\ 2a+6a+30 & =-2 \\ 8a & =-32 \\ a & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the value of $b,$ we substitute $a=-4$ into the equation $b=2a+10$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}b & =2a+10 \\  & =2(-4)+10 \\  & =-8+10 \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $a=-4,\,b=2.$

questions.problem:
Find the solution to the following system of equations.

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-\frac{2}{7}y=2 \\ -x+\frac{2}{9}y=2\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To get rid of fractions, we multiply the first equation by $7$ and the second equation by $9,$ as follows:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-\frac{2}{7}y=2 & |\times 7 \\ -x+\frac{2}{9}y=2 & |\times 9\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}7x-2y=14 \\ -9x+2y=18\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the elimination method to solve the system. We can eliminate $y$ by adding the two equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}7x-\cancel{2y} & =14 \\ -9x+\cancel{2y} & =18 \\ (7x-9x) & =(14+18) \\ -2x & =32 \\ x & =-16\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $x=-16$ into the first equation to solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}7x-2y & =14 \\ 7(-16)-2y & =14 \\ -112-2y & =14 \\ -2y & =126 \\ y & =-63\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system is $x=-16$ and $y=-63.$

questions.problem:
Find the solution to the  following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}x-\frac{1}{4}y=-1 \\ \frac{1}{3}x+\frac{1}{2}y=-6\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To get rid of fractions, we multiply the first equation by $4$ and the second equation by $6,$ as follows:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}x-\frac{1}{4}y=-1 & |\times 4 \\ \frac{1}{3}x+\frac{1}{2}y=-6 & |\times 6\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}2x-y=-4 \\ 2x+3y=-36\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the elimination method to solve the system. Notice that if we multiply the first equation by $-1,$ then we will get a $-2x$ term that can cancel with the $2x$ term in the second equation:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x-y=-4 & |\,\times (-1) \\ 2x+3y=-36 & \end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}-2x+y=4 \\ 2x+3y=-36\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the two equations eliminates the $x$-variable, and allows us to solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\cancel{-2x}+y & =4 \\ \cancel{2x}+3y & =-36 \\ (y+3y) & =(4-36) \\ 4y & =-32 \\ y & =-\frac{32}{4} \\ y & =-8\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=-8$ into the first equation to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-y & =-4 \\ 2x-(-8) & =-4 \\ 2x+8 & =-4 \\ 2x & =-12 \\ x & =-\frac{12}{2} \\ x & =-6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system is $x=-6,\,y=-8.$

$$

To get rid of the fractions in the second equation, we must multiply the second equation by the lowest common denominator of the fractions, which is $3.$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-5y=7 \\ \frac{2x}{3}+4y=-\frac{8}{3} & |\,\times 3\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}x-5y=7 \\ 2x+12y=-8\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the substitution method to solve the system. Let's solve for $x$ in the first equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-5y & =7 \\ x & =5y+7\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we can substitute $x=5y+7$ into the second equation and solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+12y & =-8 \\ 2(5y+7)+12y & =-8 \\ 10y+14+12y & =-8 \\ 22y+14 & =-8 \\ 22y & =-22 \\ y & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the value of $x,$ we substitute $y=-1$ into the equation $x=5y+7,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =5y+7 \\  & =5(-1)+7 \\  & =-5+7 \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $x=2,\,y=-1.$

questions.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{4}p+3q=25 \\ p+\frac{2}{5}q=0\end{aligned}
$$

$p=$
{{field-1}}$,\,q=$
{{field-2}}
questions.worked_solution:
To get rid of fractions, we multiply the first equation by $4$ and the second equation by $5,$ as follows:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{4}p+3q=25 & |\times 4 \\ p+\frac{2}{5}q=0 & |\times 5\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}5p+12q=100 \\ 5p+2q=0\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the elimination method to solve the system. Notice that if we multiply the first equation by $-1,$ then we will get a $-5p$ term that can cancel with the $5p$ term in the second equation:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}5p+12q=100 & |\,\times (-1) \\ 5p+2q=0 & \end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}-5p-12q=-100 \\ 5p+2q=0\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the two equations eliminates the $p$-variable, and allows us to solve for $q:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\cancel{-5p}-12q & =-100 \\ \cancel{5p}+2q & =0 \\ (-12q+2q) & =(-100+0) \\ -10q & =-100 \\ q & =\frac{100}{10} \\ q & =10\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $q=10$ into the second equation to solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5p+2q & =0 \\ 5p+2\cdot 10 & =0 \\ 5p+20 & =0 \\ 5p & =-20 \\ p & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system is $p=-4,\,q=10.$
